warning: Communism and capitalism are idealized coordination functions here, not complete descriptions of all historical regimes.

systems.label: Communism / labor-time coordination
systems.primary_optimization_signal: socially necessary labor time, effort, or direct time allocation
systems.scarce_resource_made_legible: human labor and available working time
systems.coordination_unit: collective plan, common ownership, or direct allocation
systems.time_horizon: potentially long, but dependent on planning and political institutions
systems.network_visibility: can see shared labor requirements better than isolated market actors, but may lose local preference and tacit information
systems.typical_externality: unpaid political, administrative, care, or dissent costs hidden inside the collective plan
systems.failure_mode: bureaucratic rigidity, informational compression, coercive allocation, or labor-time reductionism
systems.freedom_risk: the collective can become the employer/planner with weak exit and weak contestability
systems.correction_mechanism: participatory revision, local autonomy, plural metrics, contestable plans, and protected exit

systems.label: Capitalism / money-return coordination
systems.primary_optimization_signal: money return, profit, liquidity, or asset appreciation
systems.coordination_unit: private property, contract, price, and investment decision
systems.time_horizon: often biased toward realizable present/future cash returns
systems.network_visibility: prices aggregate some dispersed information, but may omit delayed, non-priced, or displaced costs
systems.typical_externality: care, ecological recovery, public infrastructure, unpaid coordination, and future option loss
systems.failure_mode: runaway accumulation, short-horizon optimization, concentration, crisis, and burden export
systems.freedom_risk: formal consent with dependence, lock-in, unequal exit, or employer/asset-owner domination
systems.correction_mechanism: regulation, taxation, public provision, labor power, redistribution, and institutional redesign

systems.label: Network economy / multi-resource relation pricing
systems.primary_optimization_signal: joint preservation of money, time, energy, information, and future option sets
systems.scarce_resource_made_legible: the relationship between resources, not one resource alone
systems.coordination_unit: receipted relationships, distributed ledgers, bounded local autonomy, and network-temporal feedback
systems.time_horizon: explicitly intertemporal; future recipients are included in the objective
systems.network_visibility: attempts to measure receiver-side and delayed costs through network-relative observation
systems.typical_externality: residuals are the costs that remain outside local metrics after network and temporal accounting
systems.failure_mode: measurement overload, false precision, surveillance, governance capture, or unbounded system scope
systems.freedom_risk: the metric layer can become a new planner unless assumptions, consent, exit, and contestability are explicit
systems.correction_mechanism: multi-objective accounting, adversarial residual search, future-protective constraints, and reversible governance

relationships.relation: adds omitted temporal and network costs to money coordination
retains direct labor/time visibility while rejecting labor-time sufficiency
tests whether price signals encode delayed and distributed costs
tests whether collective plans encode local information, dissent, and care burden

core_hypothesis: A network economy is not simply capitalism plus more variables. It is a proposed accounting regime in which the object of optimization is a relationship among money, time, energy, information, and future option sets.
necessary_test: The network model must outperform single-resource baselines on a held-out burden-allocation task without increasing coercion, unmeasured administrative burden, or false precision.
falsifiers: A money-only or labor-time-only baseline captures the same delayed and distributed burdens at equal or lower measurement cost.
Adding resource dimensions does not improve held-out burden prediction or allocation quality.
The network metric's apparent gains disappear under time-shuffled, node-shuffled, or boundary-perturbed controls.
The model improves accounting but increases surveillance, administrative labor, or planner power beyond the declared threshold.
Future-protective weighting systematically worsens present and future outcomes under a preregistered objective.
